messages:
maya: :rotating_light: autopager fired for host-gpu-124 (us-east-1b)
incident-bot: PAGE -> host-gpu-124: kubelet not ready / node unreachable (autopage policy v3). PagerDuty incident created: PD#INC-5921
pd-bot: Escalation policy: oncall-sre -> level2 -> infra-leads. Pager sent to maya, santiago
maya: ack. I'm attaching serial console, checking kernel messages. quick status: some pods already evicted, host stopped responding to kubelet health probe
santiago: oncall-sre here, pairing with maya. can you confirm if this is a transient I/O stall or a kernel oops? both need different playbooks
maya: grabbing dmesg from serial:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU fault detected: Xid 79, pid=0, ctx=0x0
[ 1234.568000] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 00000000
[ 1234.568123] CPU: 3 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/3 Not tainted 5.15.0-rc
```
maya: looks like kernel oops following an I/O hang. NVME I/O errors earlier in logs
lee: paging in. if it's kernel oops, we should cordon this node and drain any remaining workloads. prepare for host reboot and potential RMA
tim: customer-success FYI: we might see transient errors for customers on hosted inference in us-east-1b. No broad outage yet but v1 endpoints to region-us-east-1b may see 502/504s while pods reschedule
customer-success: noted. I'll flag paying customers with active sessions > 50k tokens and ask support to prepare proactive outreach if their requests error
santiago: cordon + drain then. executing:
```
kubectl cordon host-gpu-124
kubectl drain host-gpu-124 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
maya: running drain. a couple of stateful pods taking long to terminate (redis replicas). adding eviction grace override
santiago: set taint to prevent scheduling: kubectl taint nodes host-gpu-124 critical=kernel:NoSchedule
incident-bot: Host health check: serial console attached -> unresponsive to kernel prompt after oops. Reboot required. Suggested action: evict, reboot, collect coredump
pd-bot: PD#INC-5921 -> acknowledged by maya at 4101234572. Escalation to level2 if not resolved in 15m
maya: confirming impact metrics: about 2.8% of requests to generation API hit the failing rack, tail latency increased to 1.2s at p99 due to retries. Redirecting routing to dedicated-pool-3 for critical tiers
lee: executing flow to shift critical traffic: update routing policy to prefer region-us-east-1a/dedicated-pool-3 for model small-v2
tim: note for postmortem: check autoscaler behavior — we saw slow reschedule because of affinity rules on redis pods
santiago: ops note: we attempted a soft reboot via IPMI but node did not come back; scheduling RMA with hw-team. serial logs show repeated NVME errors -> likely hardware fault
maya: collecting snapshots: /var/crash captured, uploading to S3 (s3://redwood-ops/incident/4101234567)
customer-success: preparing templated email for impacted customers, will wait for final severity classification
oncall-sre: taking over handoff at 4101234800. maya, please leave your checklist in the incident doc and assign follow-ups: RMA ticket, kernel-oom investigation, routing rollback test
maya: leaving checklist: 1) evacuate node (done) 2) collect logs + coredump (uploading) 3) mark node unschedulable and taint (done) 4) open RMA (in progress) 5) notify CS (done)
lee: RMA created: RMA-8812, ETA on replacement hardware 48-72h. For short term we'll keep node cordoned and rely on fallback pools
santiago: marking incident severity: SEV-2 (customer-impact but partial, short-lived). will draft timeline for postmortem
pd-bot: PD#INC-5921 -> resolved (auto) at 4101234975 after node cordoned and critical traffic shifted. If issue recurs, page will reopen
oncall-sre: handoff complete. leaving thread for postmortem notes and timeline updates. please @mention me for any follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
maya: thx everyone. I'll add kernel oops stack traces to the incident doc and schedule a deeper infra blameless review tomorrow.
